clue.text: It's necessary to describe somebody as a slattern

indicators.note: the letters needed are part of the run of words that follows, so the solver must look inside them

explanation.surface: A writer feels obliged to call some unkempt woman a slattern.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'descriBE SOMebody'; the indicator 'necessary to' is loose, saying the letters are required from within those words. 'describe' looks like the verb of the sentence but is part of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides meaning a broom of twigs, the word is an old dialect term for a slovenly, untidy woman.

clue.text: Supports the Archbishop, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: to back is to support, so supports is backs
Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1928 to 1942

explanation.surface: Someone stands behind the Archbishop, in a figurative sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Back slang is a British form of slang made by saying words backwards, as 'yob' from 'boy'. 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a throwaway phrase but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Back slang is a slang language formed by reversing words, so a way of talking.

clue.text: Gather some herbs, including rosemary, ready for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A cook picks herbs, rosemary among them, for the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' looks like a meal course but takes the first letter of each of the five words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: In sewing, to shirr is to gather cloth into parallel rows of puckers.

clue.text: Devious routes and ways to take in the alien

indicators.note: the word for ways encloses the foreign article

parts.note: means are ways of doing something
der is German for the, a foreign version of the word

explanation.surface: Winding paths and strategies for bringing in an extraterrestrial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the alien' is not a spaceman but 'the' in a foreign language, German DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanders are winding, roundabout courses, like a river's loops.

clue.text: Leave fool to rule after end of Yule

indicators.note: the word for rule comes after the letter taken from Yule

parts.note: a goon is a stupid or foolish person

indicators.note: the final letter of the word Yule is the one wanted

parts.note: to hold sway is to rule

explanation.surface: Someone is told to let a fool take charge once the Christmas season is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes E from Yule; 'after' puts SWAY behind that E.
explanation.definitionFit: To go one's own way is to depart and follow an independent course, so it means to leave.

clue.text: Leave one fellow out — he's a fool

indicators.note: one letter is left out of the phrase for leave

parts.note: to go off is to leave
F is the abbreviation for fellow, and only one of the two is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone is told to exclude a man because he is an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: GO OFF has two Fs; 'one fellow out' removes just one.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is a silly or clumsy person, a dope.

clue.text: When you can hunt one, pass one out

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunter is told to let one prey go past during the permitted season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' looks like the object of 'hunt', but both 'one's and 'pass' are the anagram fodder for 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Open season is the period of the year when shooting or hunting a given animal is legally allowed.

clue.text: Departure from America, after the party's over

indicators.note: the abbreviation for America comes after the turned party

parts.note: ex means from, as in ex works

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for party is turned over, reading upwards

parts.note: a do is a party
US is short for United States

explanation.surface: Leaving the United States once the celebrations have ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns DO to OD; 'after' puts US at the end. EX for 'from' is the Latin preposition seen in 'ex works'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exodus is a mass departure, named for the Israelites leaving Egypt.

clue.text: Record the reduction in value

explanation.surface: An accountant notes down a drop in an asset's worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To write down is to note something on paper; as a noun, a write-down is an accounting cut in an asset's book value.

clue.text: As yet uncertain, in ferment

indicators.note: the order of the letters is not settled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Matters are still undecided and in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ferment' reads as agitation; it is the agent that causes fermentation.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus that makes dough rise and beer brew, a classic fermenting agent.

clue.text: What happened in the Boxer Rebellion? A bloomer

definitions.text: What happened in the Boxer Rebellion?

explanation.surface: A history question followed by a mischievous answer about a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Boxer Rebellion of 1900 China rose up against foreign powers; read as a noun the same words name a flowering shrub. 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: First sense: the nation of China rose in revolt; second sense: a flowering shrub of the hibiscus or rose family, a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Novelist who is bilingual? Yes

parts.note: yes said in French is oui
yes said in Russian is da, the second of the two languages

explanation.surface: A question about whether a certain writer spoke two languages, answered in the affirmative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bilingual' tells you to say yes in two languages: French OUI and Russian DA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouida was the pen name of Maria Louise Ramé, a Victorian writer of popular romantic fiction.

clue.text: The way to travel — walk

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ride is to travel on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone declares walking to be the best way to get about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The way to travel' reads as one phrase but splits into way (ST) and travel (RIDE).
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long step, and to stride is to walk with long steps.

clue.text: Uncle set out for something to eat

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order, freely rearranged

explanation.surface: An uncle lays out a meal for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' looks like a phrasal verb; only 'out' signals the anagram of UNCLE SET.
explanation.definitionFit: An esculent is anything edible, a foodstuff fit for eating.

clue.text: Large vehicle out of control bearing a writer

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, extra large
a car is a vehicle
wild means unruly, out of control
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A big runaway lorry carrying an author.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a clothing label for large sizes; 'bearing' gives a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was the Irish playwright and wit behind The Importance of Being Earnest.

clue.text: A second reading incorporates university, in accordance with custom

indicators.note: the word for reading takes the university letter into its body

parts.note: a perusal is a careful reading

explanation.surface: Someone reading a text again finds a university included, as always.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporates' puts U inside PERUSAL, making PERUSUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: As per usual is a jokey phrase for the way things normally go, following habit.

clue.text: Everyone standing up given sauce for pout

indicators.note: in a down clue standing makes the words read upwards, backwards

parts.note: all means everyone
taken as written
sauce and face both mean cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: A whole audience rises and a cheeky retort makes someone sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns ALL UP into PULLA. FACE, like sauce, means impudence: 'the face to ask'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a face is to grimace, and a pout is a sulky grimace.

clue.text: In the which one's up the creek, well up

definitions.text: In the which one's up the creek

parts.note: so and well both open a remark, as in so, what next
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled-looking remark about someone stuck without a paddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in: 'In the ___' is where one is when up the creek, that is, in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the soup is an idiom for being in trouble, the same plight as being up the creek.

clue.text: Sap exuded can be collected using these steps

indicators.note: the letters are gathered up and composed in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Tree sap that oozes out can be gathered by following a method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steps' looks like a procedure for gathering sap but means dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas de deux is a ballet sequence of dance moves for two performers.

clue.text: Leading seaman gets heartless, order to abandon

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor, and he leads, placed first

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for order is removed

parts.note: to dictate is to give orders

explanation.surface: A senior sailor gets a cruel command to leave ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle T of DICTATE, giving DICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to renounce or give up a throne or duty.

clue.text: Hit back and :'t game

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Hit back and :'t game (4)'; the scan blots the word after 'and', so the clue cannot be given as printed (GOLF is FLOG reversed, but the full text is missing).

clue.text: What you might call a beanpole with, below, 4 b-beans entwined

definitions.text: What you might call a beanpole

indicators.note: the letters are twisted together into a new order

parts.note: the clue below 4 across is 4 down, whose answer is goof
the stuttered b-beans gives B plus BEANS

explanation.surface: Someone labels a tall thin person after twining stammered beans round a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below, 4' means the down clue numbered 4 (GOOF); add BBEANS from the stammer and 'entwined' rearranges all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of bones is a very thin person, just as a beanpole is a tall skinny one.

clue.text: I was a prince, though I was succeeded by a king

definitions.text: I was a prince, though I was succeeded by a king

parts.words: I was a prince, though I was succeeded by a king
parts.note: Victoria's consort was only ever a prince, yet the son who came after him, also given that first name, became King Edward VII

explanation.surface: A royal speaker muses that a king followed him though he never wore a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria's husband held the title Prince Consort, never king; their son Albert Edward reigned as Edward VII.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert, the husband of Queen Victoria, was a prince whose eldest son became a monarch.

clue.text: Mum lets people wade here

parts.note: mum as in keep mum is silent, which is sh
to allow is to let, so lets is allows

explanation.surface: A mother permits folk to paddle in a certain spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not a mother here but the call for silence, SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallows are stretches of shallow water, where people can paddle on foot.

clue.text: Rock music

explanation.surface: A two-word note on a musical genre.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock is to sway back and forth; swing is also a jazz style of the big-band era.

clue.text: In confusion deserter and robber .

indicators.note: the word for deserter sits inside the word for confusion

parts.note: pie is a printer's term for jumbled type, hence a state of confusion
a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: In a chaotic scene a runaway and a thief appear.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE (or pi) is printers' slang for type spilled into a jumble. The clue runs on into 26 across, where the same answer loses a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate robs ships at sea.

clue.text: A bit of canvas hoisted under another name

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is lifted up, reading upwards

parts.note: a sail is a piece of canvas

explanation.surface: A sheet of canvas is run up a mast under a false flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoisted' turns SAIL to LIAS beneath A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alias, as an adverb, means otherwise known as, going by a different name.

clue.text: Animal's food supply cut

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off the word for food supply

parts.note: board is daily meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A beast's rations are reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the final D of BOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a male pig or wild pig.

clue.text: . dropping money becomes incensed

indicators.note: a letter is let fall from the word carried over

parts.note: the dots continue from 23 across, whose answer is the sea robber
p is the abbreviation for penny, a coin of money

explanation.surface: A thief who loses his loot flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening dots carry on from 23 across: that robber, 'dropping' P (a penny), leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, furious.

clue.text: Double 1000 ÷ 200 and be quick about it

indicators.note: K stands for a thousand; divide by two hundred and you get five, the Roman V, so one letter swaps for the other

parts.note: a double is a person who looks just like another, a lookalike

explanation.surface: A sum to work out quickly before someone demands haste.
explanation.walkthrough: K is 1000 (as in kilo) and V is the Roman five; 1000 ÷ 200 = 5, so the K in LOOKALIKE becomes V.
explanation.definitionFit: Look alive is a command to hurry up and be alert.

clue.text: Dipper in jar uncovered, we hear

indicators.note: the words are said aloud and sound like the answer

parts.note: to jar is to grate, as a noise grates on the nerves; something uncovered is bare

explanation.surface: A ladle is found in an open jar, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dipper' looks like a ladle or bird; it is the star pattern, called the Big Dipper in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation Ursa Major contains the seven stars known as the Plough or Big Dipper.

clue.text: Cricket team takes two points, ends on 17

parts.note: east and south are two points of the compass, E and S
the last letters of the three words making up 17 down, PAS, DE, DEUX

explanation.surface: A side scores two points, finishing on seventeen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends on 17' takes the final letter of each word of 17 down's answer: S, E, X. ESSEX is an English county, which fields a first-class cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex County Cricket Club plays in England's county championship.
